dossier.orientation: Simple Analytics is a cookie-free website analytics option for agencies and freelance developers evaluating a repeatable default across client sites, with per-site installation and documented privacy conditions.

setup_conditions: Add each website and use the technology-detected HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option.

Which Self-serve account roles or client-access arrangements are available for agency-to-client handoff?
How do plan pricing and limits aggregate when an agency installs Simple Analytics across a larger client-site portfolio?
defining_need_fit.supported_core_workflow: A standard, easy-to-recommend, cookie-free analytics default that avoids DPA/consent-banner friction across many client sites.
defining_need_fit.caveat: The documented per-site installation and privacy behavior support an exploratory product evaluation across client builds, but R15 describes the additional-website rule in a subdomain context and does not establish the Self-serve site cap or aggregate portfolio cost; the research also does not verify firsthand agency demand or recipient qualification.
defining_need_fit.why: Official documentation supports the required combination of no cookies or visitor consent, no DPA under the stated GDPR basis, EU data storage, a limited non-personal data scope, and repeatable technology-dependent installation for added websites.

ranked_relevance.why: Directly supports the defining cookie-free and consent-banner-avoidance requirement by documenting no cookies, trackers or required visitor consent.
Directly supports the DPA-friction requirement, conditioned on the documented absence of personal-data processing and GDPR's definition of when a DPA is required.
Documents the repeatable installation mechanism: each site is scanned and receives technology-dependent code or another platform-specific option.
Defines the processed data scope—Page URL, Referrer, UTM parameters, Time zone, and Device and browser type—processed in the EU and not linked to identifiable users.
Establishes EU storage with primary infrastructure in the Netherlands, an explicit required capability for this audience definition.

Supports multi-website evaluation because additional websites do not cost extra individually, subject to a plan-wide limit and the fact that the statement appears in a subdomain context rather than explicitly covering arbitrary client domains.
Provides a concrete commercial reference: €20/month on monthly billing at about 100k monthly pageviews, with price scaling and two months free on annual billing.
The Free plan's five-website cap, one-user limit, one-month history and required badge make it a poor primary fact for a professional default across client sites.

problem_fits.caveat: These sources document Simple Analytics' own behavior and stated GDPR basis; they do not establish a universal legal conclusion for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
problem_fits.why: The product documentation directly addresses the dispute for this product through no cookies, no trackers, no required visitor consent and no personal-data processing under its stated data scope.

problem_fits.caveat: The paid Self-serve reference and constrained Free plan permit cost evaluation but do not show that the economics are acceptable across many client sites; P2 is also single-source and its current applicability is unknown.
problem_fits.why: Documented prices and multi-website billing behavior address components of the cost concern without proving parity with free GA or suitability for an agency portfolio.
